newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TRACTEBEL, SUEZ LYONNAISE NO COMPETITORS - MESTRALLET.
newsitem.headline: TRACTEBEL, SUEZ LYONNAISE NO COMPETITORS - MESTRALLET.

text.p: Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA and its French parent Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux will not compete with each other, directors of the French group told a Belgian newspaper.

"I think it is wrong to qualify the relationship between Tractebel and Lyonnaise des Eaux as a competitive one. The former does not want to become a player in the water business, while the latter only has a small presence in electricity," Suez chief executive officer Gerard Mestrallet told Le Soir.
"There is no question of clipping Tractebel's wings, Belgian or international," Lyonnaise head Jerome Monod told Le Soir.

On Friday, holding company Suez and utilities group Lyonnaise announced their intention to merge. Suez owns 63 percent of Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) which in turn owns 65 percent of Tractebel.
The merger plan has led to worries in Belgium that Tractebel's expansion would be arrested by Lyonnaise.

"The world market is vast, and I believe there will be neither conflict of interest or overlap between the two groups. There will probably be a coordination of the expansion ambitions, but no contradiction," Monod added.
